stem: During the preoperative team briefing for a planned minimally invasive procedure, the surgeon states that conversion to an open procedure may be necessary. The circulating nurse realizes that the open-procedure instrument set is not immediately available. What is the best action?

options.A: Begin the procedure because conversion can be discussed only if it actually becomes necessary
options.B: Use the briefing to communicate the resource gap and ensure required open-procedure equipment is available before the case begins
options.C: Wait until conversion is requested, then leave the room to locate the needed equipment
options.D: Omit the concern from the briefing because equipment availability is unrelated to team communication

rationale: AORN team-communication guidance identifies briefings as a tool for creating a shared mental model and situational awareness. AORN minimally invasive surgery guidance specifically notes that discussing possible conversion to an open procedure during the preoperative briefing allows the team to identify and gather needed resources in advance and anticipate intraoperative changes. Starting without required resources or waiting until an urgent conversion is underway creates avoidable delay and risk.
educational_objective: Use preoperative briefings to identify anticipated changes in the surgical plan and close resource gaps before the procedure begins, especially when conversion to an open procedure is possible.
source_document_title: Revised Guideline for Team Communication; Updates to the Guideline for Minimally Invasive Surgery
source_version_date: Team Communication revision published 2024-07-09; current in AORN Guidelines for Perioperative Practice, 2026 Edition
source_locator: Team Communication — briefings promote a shared mental model and situational awareness; Minimally Invasive Surgery, Communication/Key Takeaway — discuss potential conversion to open procedure during preoperative briefing to identify and gather resources in advance
source_claim_supported: AORN supports preoperative briefing to create shared situational awareness and specifically recommends discussing possible open conversion so the team can identify and gather resources in advance.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team / Continuity of Care: identify significant information to report; communicate with team; utilize resources to promote quality client care
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — team communication and resource coordination
correction_summary: Converted a definition-style briefing item into a concrete resource-readiness decision. The final scenario tests why team briefing matters clinically and uses a directly supported AORN conversion-to-open example.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: AORN 2024 revised Team Communication guidance and minimally invasive conversion guidance verified; 2026 AORN edition confirms current guideline set.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Briefing/shared mental model and advance resource gathering for possible open conversion are directly supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; briefing is intended to anticipate, not defer, foreseeable needs.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; addresses the identified resource gap before risk materializes.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; waiting for urgent conversion creates avoidable delay.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; resource readiness and communication are explicitly linked in AORN guidance.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B uses the briefing to proactively resolve the stated risk.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern timing and use of the briefing.
audit_findings.blueprint: Direct NCSBN 2026 Management of Care team/resource coordination alignment.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked whether open-set presence is universally mandatory; stem states surgeon anticipates possible conversion, making advance availability a directly supported case-specific action rather than a universal rule.
